day-1.t: Day 1 — How marketplace selling really works

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand what Daraz does and what you do
Know where your money goes before it reaches you
Decide whether a marketplace suits your product

b.v: About 15 minutes. Keep the seller centre open in a browser tab.

Daraz is a marketplace, not a shop builder. You list products inside their system, they bring the buyers and handle most of the delivery, and they take a cut. You do not own the customer relationship the way you do on your own website, and that single fact shapes everything else.
1) Who does what
Knowing the split stops most beginner frustration. Some things you control, some you only influence.

v: You control: product, price, stock, photos, description, packaging
They control: the storefront, the traffic, the courier network, the payment collection
You handle: dispatch on time, answer buyer messages, accept returns per policy
They handle: collecting the cash and paying you on a settlement cycle

b.v: 2) Where the money goes
Every sale has deductions before it reaches your bank. The exact figures change often and differ by category, so treat any number you hear from another seller as a starting point only.

v: Commission, a percentage of the selling price
Shipping fee charged to the seller, which varies by weight and city
Payment processing or other service charges, if applicable
Penalties for late dispatch or cancelled orders, when they apply

b.v: Do not set prices from a screenshot of fees you saw last year. Open the seller centre and read the current commission and shipping tables for your category before you list anything.
3) Is your product a fit
Marketplaces reward certain products and punish others. Being honest now saves a wasted month.

v: Good fit: light, hard to break, easy to describe, searched by many people
Poor fit: fragile, very heavy, needs fitting or a demo
Poor fit: products where buyers must feel the quality first
Poor fit: very low margin items, because fees eat the profit

b.v: Practice
Search your product on Daraz today. Write down the first ten prices you see, the number of reviews each listing has, and whether you can beat them after fees.

day-2.t: Day 2 — Open the seller account properly

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand the onboarding steps in general terms
Prepare documents before you start
Avoid the mistakes that delay approval

b.v: About 25 minutes. Have your documents and bank details ready.

Onboarding is a form, a verification and a wait. The flow changes from time to time, and the current steps are always shown on the seller signup page and in the seller centre, so follow what is there today rather than a video from two years ago.
1) What you usually need
The exact list is shown during signup. These are the things almost every seller has to produce in some form.

v: A phone number and email you check daily
Your national identity document, with the name matching your bank account
A bank account in your own name for settlements
Business details, if you have a registered business
A shop name that is not copying an existing brand

b.v: 2) The signup flow
Read every screen. Most rejections come from a mismatch between the name on the identity document and the name on the bank account.

In general terms:|Open the seller signup page and create an account|Verify the phone number and email|Fill your personal and business details exactly as printed on your documents|Add the bank account for payouts|Upload clear photos of the required documents|Choose your category and submit for review|Wait for approval before you list, and check email for questions
Never open a second seller account because the first is stuck in review. Duplicate accounts are usually merged or blocked, and you can lose both.
3) Get ready while you wait
Approval is a good time to prepare, so you can list on day one instead of starting from zero.

v: Photograph five products on a plain background
Write descriptions in your own words
Buy packaging material in bulk
Decide your dispatch routine and who covers it on Fridays

b.v: Practice
Make a folder on your phone with clear photos of your identity document and bank details, then write down the exact name printed on each one. All four names must match.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Create a listing that gets approved

b.v: Today's goal

v: Create one listing from scratch
Fill every field the system scores
Get it approved on the first try

b.v: About 25 minutes. Have photos ready on the same device.
A listing is a form, not a poster. Approval depends on correct category, correct attributes and honest images. Sales depend on the title, the first photo and the price. Both matter, in that order.
1) Choose the right category
Category decides which attributes you must fill, which filters shoppers use, and which commission applies. A wrong category is the most common reason a good product never sells.

v: Search your exact product and see which category the top sellers sit in
Prefer the deepest specific category, not the general one
Do not list in a category just because commission looks lower
Check the category rules for restricted items

b.v: 2) Fill the listing form
Fill every field, even optional ones. Empty attributes mean your product never appears when a buyer uses filters.

Create it:|Seller centre, then Products, then Add product|Pick the category and confirm the suggested attributes|Type the title using the formula in Day 4|Upload at least five images, first one on a plain background|Fill brand, model, size, colour, material, package contents|Write the description and the warranty line if you offer one|Set price, stock and dispatch time, then submit
Do not put words like cheap, best price or sale in the title. Many marketplaces treat title spam as a quality violation, and buyers ignore it anyway.
3) If it is rejected
Rejection is normal and fixable. Read the reason instead of resubmitting the same file and hoping.

v: Image rejected: usually a watermark, logo or text on the photo
Category rejected: the item sits in the wrong place
Brand rejected: you claimed a brand you cannot prove
Description rejected: copied text or contact details inside the listing

b.v: Practice
Create one listing today and submit it. Write down the rejection reason if there is one, then fix exactly that field and resubmit once.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Titles, images and words that sell

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write a title that matches how people search
Build a five photo set that answers questions
Rewrite one existing listing

b.v: About 20 minutes. Use your phone, no studio needed.

Marketplace search is mostly text matching. The buyer types words, and the listing that contains those words in a sensible order appears. Then the first photo decides the click, and the rest of the photos decide the sale.
1) The title formula
Put the words a buyer types first, then the specifics. Keep it readable, because a person still has to understand it in one second.

v: Brand, then product type, then key attribute, then size or quantity
Example shape: Brand Cotton Bedsheet Set Double Bed 3 Pieces
Use the words buyers use, not factory words
No emojis, no repeated words, no shop name

b.v: 2) The five photo set
Photos do the explaining. Plan them as answers to questions, not as decoration.

Shoot these five:|Front view on a plain white or light background|Side or back view, to show shape|Close up of the material or finish|The product in use, with a hand or a person for scale|Everything that comes in the box, laid out
Do not use the supplier's photos if they show a brand you do not own, and never put your phone number or shop name on an image. Both get listings removed.
3) Description that prevents returns
A good description does not oversell. It sets exact expectations, so the parcel that arrives matches the promise and does not come back.

v: What is included, with quantity
Exact measurements in centimetres, not only words like large
Material and care instructions
Warranty or return line, matching the platform policy
No contact details, no links, no other shop names

b.v: Practice
Rewrite the title of one of your listings using the formula, and reshoot the first photo on a plain background. Compare the two side by side before you replace anything.

day-5.t: Day 5 — Price with commission and shipping in mind

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build a price from cost upwards, not from competitors downwards
Include commission and shipping in the calculation
Set a floor price you will not break

b.v: About 20 minutes. A calculator and your cost sheet.

On a marketplace the visible price is not your income. Commission and shipping are deducted first, and both are percentages or slabs that change. So build your price from the bottom and check the current deductions in the seller centre.
1) Build the price upwards
Start with what the item really costs you, add the deductions, then add your profit. Never start by copying the cheapest competitor.

Calculate like this:|Product cost, including delivery to you|Packaging cost per parcel|Shipping charge you will pay, read the current table|Commission percentage for your category, read the current table|Add your target profit|The total is your list price, round it to a clean number
2) Compete without destroying the margin
If your calculated price is far above the market, the product is wrong, not the price. Do not fix a bad product with a loss making price.

v: Compare like for like: same size, same quantity, same material
Look at listings with reviews, those are proven sellers
Never price below your floor, no matter what a competitor does
Differentiate with bundle quantity instead of cutting price

b.v: Do not join a price war on a product you cannot source cheaper. You will sell a lot, work hard, and end the month with less money than you started.
3) Write your floor price down
A floor is the lowest price that still pays you. Writing it in your notebook stops panic discounting during a campaign.

v: Floor = all costs plus a minimum profit you accept
Never go under it for a flash sale
Recheck the floor whenever fees change
If a campaign forces below floor, sit that campaign out

b.v: Practice
Calculate the full price for your main product using today's commission and shipping figures from the seller centre. Write the floor price in your notebook and sign it with the date.
Today's goal

v: Keep stock counts honest
Set a dispatch routine you can repeat daily
Avoid the two mistakes that cause penalties

b.v: About 20 minutes. Do this before your first order arrives.
On a marketplace, a late dispatch is not a small delay. It counts against your seller score, and repeated problems can limit your listings. A boring daily routine is the whole solution.
1) Keep stock honest
Overselling is worse than being out of stock. A cancelled order costs you a penalty and the buyer's trust at the same time.

v: Update the count every evening, after packing
Keep a buffer for damaged items in your own stock
Turn a listing off when stock is zero, do not leave it live
Count physical stock once a week against the system

b.v: 2) The daily routine
Same steps, same time, every working day. Boring is profitable here.

Every morning:|Open the seller centre and check new orders|Print or note the labels and pack in order of dispatch deadline|Book the pickup or drop the parcels at the collection point|Mark orders as ready in the system|Reply to buyer messages before packing ends
Do not mark an order as shipped before the parcel is actually with the courier. It hides a problem from the system and creates a worse one when the buyer asks where it is.
3) Reply fast, reply short
Response time is measured, and buyers who get a fast answer are less likely to cancel. Keep replies to two lines.

v: Answer within the same working day
Use saved replies for the five common questions
Never argue about a return in messages, follow the policy
Never ask a buyer to pay outside the platform

b.v: Practice
Write your daily dispatch routine on a card and stick it where you pack. Then set two phone alarms, one for orders and one for messages.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Packaging that survives the courier

b.v: Today's goal

v: Pack so the product arrives undamaged
Keep the parcel light and small
Add the small touches that earn a good rating

b.v: About 20 minutes. Pack one real parcel as practice.
A parcel passes through several hands and a truck. Damage means a return, a refund and a bad rating, all for the price of a piece of bubble wrap. Packaging is the cheapest insurance you can buy.
1) The three layer rule
Product protection, then a water layer, then a strong outer box or bag. Skip one layer and you will learn the lesson the expensive way.

v: Inner: bubble wrap or foam around the product itself
Middle: a poly bag so rain and dust stay out
Outer: a proper box or tough courier bag, taped on all seams
Label flat, on the largest surface, never on a corner

b.v: 2) Keep weight and size down
Shipping is charged on weight and sometimes on size. Padding that is too generous costs money on every single order.

Pack efficiently:|Weigh the bare product first and note it|Choose the smallest box that fits with padding|Fill empty space with paper, not with extra bubble wrap|Weigh the finished parcel and compare with your estimate|Adjust the box choice if the weight jumped
Do not send liquids or glass in a plain poly bag. One break in transit becomes a refund, a return shipping charge and a one star rating.
3) The unboxing moment
The buyer judges the whole order in the ten seconds after opening. Small cheap touches lift ratings, which lift sales.

v: A printed thank you slip with the order number
The product wrapped neatly, not thrown in
A care instruction card for clothing
No price slips from your supplier left inside

b.v: Practice
Pack one parcel properly today, weigh it, and drop it from waist height onto a soft floor. If anything moves or rattles inside, repack it.
Today's goal

v: Understand why returns happen and what they cost
Handle a return without damaging your score
Cut the two causes you control

b.v: About 20 minutes. Read the current return policy in the seller centre.

Marketplace returns are usually buyer friendly, and that is part of why people buy there. You cannot remove that risk, but you can lower it. A returned parcel costs you the forward shipping, the return shipping and the lost sale.
1) Know the rules you agreed to
Return windows, who pays return shipping, and which categories are excluded all change over time. Read the current policy rather than repeating what another seller told you.

v: Check the return window length for your category
Check which reasons count as seller fault
Check what happens to the shipping fee on a return
Check the appeal process and the time limit for raising one

b.v: 2) When a return arrives
Stay calm and follow the process. Arguing in messages makes a small case into a complaint.

Handle it like this:|Read the reason carefully and check the order photos|Accept the return if it is within policy|Respond to the buyer in two polite lines|Inspect the item when it comes back, photograph it|Raise an appeal only if the policy clearly supports you
Do not refuse a valid return to save one parcel's cost. The penalty and the rating damage cost more than the item.
3) Cut returns at the source
Most returns in this market come from expectation gaps, not from broken products. Fix the listing and the gap closes.

v: Wrong size: publish exact measurements in centimetres
Wrong colour: show the real colour, no heavy filters
Poor quality: do not stock the cheapest grade
Damaged: improve the packaging from Day 7

b.v: Practice
Open your best selling listing and add exact measurements to the description. That one change prevents the most common return reason.
Today's goal

v: Earn ratings honestly
Prepare for a campaign without losing money
Use the tools the platform gives you

b.v: About 20 minutes. Open your seller score page.
Ratings decide whether your listing appears near the top, and campaigns decide whether you get a burst of orders. Both are useful, and both can hurt you if you chase them the wrong way.
1) Ratings you can influence
You cannot control what a buyer writes. You can control the three things buyers complain about most.

v: Delivery speed, mostly decided by how fast you dispatch
Product matching the photos, decided by your honesty
Packaging condition, decided by Day 7
Reply to negative reviews once, politely, without arguing

b.v: 2) Join a campaign with a plan
A campaign is a platform promotion, often with a discounted price and sometimes a slot fee or a deeper commission. Read the terms before you press join.

Before joining:|Open the campaign terms and read the discount requirement|Check the extra fees, if any|Compare the campaign price with your floor price|Check you have enough stock for the expected volume|Join only if the campaign price stays above the floor
Do not buy fake reviews or ask friends to post five stars. It is against the rules, it is detectable, and it can cost you the account.
3) Free tools inside the seller centre
These reduce cost without spending on ads. Most sellers ignore them.

v: Bundles, to raise the average order value
Vouchers you fund yourself, with a usage limit
Free shipping thresholds, if the platform offers them
Sponsored listings, only after your organic listing converts

b.v: Practice
Reply politely to your oldest unanswered review today. Then check whether any current campaign price stays above your floor and write yes or no with the reason.

day-10.t: Day 10 — The numbers to watch every week

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build a one page weekly scorecard
Reconcile your payouts against real orders
Decide one action for the coming week

b.v: About 25 minutes. Same day every week, in a notebook.
A marketplace dashboard is full of numbers, most of which you cannot act on. Five numbers are enough for a small seller, and the most important is the one nobody checks: money actually received.
1) The five numbers
Write these every week, in the same order, so you compare like with like.

v: Orders: how many this week
Cancellations and returns: how many, and the reason
Selling price total, before deductions
Payout received, after all deductions
Rating and seller score

b.v: 2) Reconcile the payout
The gap between what you sold and what you received is where mistakes hide. Check it line by line once a week.

Reconcile like this:|Export the order list for the period|Open the payout statement and match order numbers|Look for commission, shipping and any penalty lines|Note any order marked delivered but missing from the payout|Raise a ticket the same week if something does not match
Do not wait three months to check payouts. Records get harder to match over time, and small deductions repeated a hundred times become a large amount.
3) One action, one week
Reading numbers without deciding anything is entertainment. Pick one weak number and one action, then check it next week.

v: Many views, few orders: fix the first photo and price
Many orders, many returns: fix sizes and photos
Good sales, low payout: recheck commission and shipping
Low views: improve keywords in the title, then consider sponsored listings

b.v: Practice
Open your payout statement and match the last ten orders by hand. Write any difference you cannot explain, then raise one ticket about it today.
